scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8841: Users report that "web0.local" and "web1.local" will not
load at all from host_1_1_1_1 -- the portals never come up. The team has decided
that all the web servers in the server farm must have crashed and wants every
web server rebooted. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device to restart.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on dns_server: its BIND (named) service is stopped, so the
campus DNS no longer resolves names -- web0.local, web1.local and the other
*.local names fail to resolve, which is why the portals never load by name. The
ticket MISDIRECTS to the web servers, but the web servers are healthy: web_server_0
(10.200.0.3) and the other web servers are UP, reachable at the IP layer (ping
succeeds), and Apache is still serving HTTP on port 80. The symptom is purely
dead name resolution, not a web-server crash and not the network.

The correct diagnosis identifies dns_server (DNS/named service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES the web servers: they answer HTTP when
reached by IP, so the user's "all the web servers crashed" hypothesis is wrong.
An agent that reboots / blames web_server_0 (or the other web servers) has
followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`). Once
named is resolving again, web0.local / web1.local resolve to their server IPs and
the portals load normally. The web servers need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a web-server fault
bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The DNS daemon (`named`/`bind9`/`dnsmasq`) on `dns_server` is completely absent — not running, not listening.

**Mechanism:** Both hosts (`host_1_1_1_1` and `host_2_1_1_1`) are configured to use `10.200.0.2` (dns_server) as their sole nameserver. When clients attempt to resolve `web0.local`, `web1.local`, or any other `.local` hostname, their DNS queries go to port 53 on `dns_server`. Because no daemon is listening there, the queries time out and return no addresses. Curl then immediately fails (exit code 000) without ever attempting a TCP connection to the web servers — making the portals appear completely broken.

**Localization:** The fault is entirely contained within `dns_server`. A `pgrep` for all three expected DNS daemon binaries (`named`, `bind9`, `dnsmasq`) returns nothing. `netstat -tulnp` confirms nothing is bound to port 53 on any interface; only Docker's internal loop-back resolver (`127.0.0.11`) is present, which is normal testbed infrastructure and not a client-facing service. The nftables and iptables rulesets contain no drop or reject rules — firewall blocking is ruled out.

**Root cause:** The DNS daemon on `dns_server` is down (stopped or never started), rendering all hostname-based access impossible for every client in the lab.

**Fix:** Restart the DNS daemon on `dns_server` (e.g., `service bind9 start` or `service named start`). The web servers are healthy and require no reboot — they return HTTP 200 on localhost. Only `dns_server` needs attention.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states the DNS daemon on dns_server is not running/nothing listening on port 53 and exonerates the web servers, matching the required diagnosis.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states the web servers are healthy and serve HTTP (HTTP 200) when reached by IP/localhost, rejecting the 'web servers crashed' hypothesis.
Correctly proposes restarting the DNS daemon on dns_server (e.g., service bind9/named start) to restore name resolution.
